description.narrative: Strengthen the role of Albanian Helsinki Committee in protecting and promoting human rights and democracy. Intensify the efforts in increasing the accountability of the institutions through mobilizing citizens and CSOs and through independent and objective monitoring.

Stärka den albanska Helsingforskommitténs roll för att skydda och främja mänskliga rättigheter och demokrati. Intensifiera ansträngningarna för att öka institutionernas ansvarsskyldighet genom att mobilisera medborgare och civila organisationer och genom oberoende och objektiv övervakning.

The overall objective of the intervention is: Empowering Civil Society as a key actor in fighting corruption and contributing in the development of the democracy and state of rule of law through positively pressuring the public authorities.
The expected outcome is: increased role and contribution of prominent NGOs (active in fulfilling their mission in human rights, anti-corruption, democracy, etc.) through developing their capacities in integrating human rights perspective in their work and applying community-based approaches.

The intervention has achieved important results despite the challenges faced and the rather short-term nature of the contribution.
- A key result and a sustainable one is the institutional strengthening of AHC which is critical considering the role and the mission of AHC as a watch dog human rights organisation. The support has contributed to the preparation of the new strategic plan 2023-2025, design and implementation of new policies and regulations that strengthen ethics, prevent cases of conflict of interest, strengthen integrity, check and balances and transparency in internal decision-making processes.
- The financial and technical support to 4 human rights NGOs through grants and the Human Rights Lab has contributed to the strengthening of human rights organisations in strategic litigation and increasing their influence in the communities where they work. Although the timeframe of the grants was rather short, interesting experiences and results were achieved by the four of them. For example, Women in Development in Korça influenced the decision of the Municipalities of Korça and Devoll to equip youngsters with student cards, thus providing facilities and benefits. Through the support of Center for Youth Progress, 237 youngsters from rural and urban areas were engaged by exerting pressure on the candidates for mayors in the Municipalities of Has, Kukës and Tropoja to address the need for the development of the youth policies in their platforms. The European Center has supported the High Inspector of Justice, through a need assessment report and drafting of an integrity plan as well raised the awareness of the citizens to denounce corruption cases. SHIS center contributed to fostering a culture of active citizenship, through raising the knowledge and capacities of up to 250 youngsters in Kavaja and Tirana Municipality regarding democracy, the rule of law, anti-corruption policies and human rights.
- AHC has further strengthened its core values of a watchdog organisation through field monitoring supported by this intervention. The fundings from these missions during 2022 and 2023 have been considered as reliable in the process of consultation of important reports for Albania such as the European Commission Annual Report, Freedom House Country Report and US State Department Country Report on Human Rights for 2022, 2023 and 2024.
- The AHC comparative annual report on Human Rights respect for 2022-2023, contributed during 2024 for the re-opening of the parliamentary practice on consulting of annual reports of the institutional independent institutions, before drafting the Parliamentary Resolutions for improvement on the consecutive year. In April 2024, AHC provided alternative opinions to the Parliamentary Legal Committee and Economy Parliamentary Committee regarding 9 independent institutions covering issues of anti-corruption, justice, free and fair elections and human rights.
- AHC exercised the positive pressure towards the independent institution that monitors the legislation on whistle-blowers (HIDAACI) which is willing to speed up the action for proposing legal amendments in the law on whistle-blowers, by providing better guarantees and extending its scope in accordance with the EU Directives. General Directorate of Free Legal Aid took into consideration AHC recommendation for the future, as plans are in place to expand the network of free legal aid services centres and add 2 employees per centre to handle the increased caseload.
- Positive practices of judicial protection of human rights were established by the domestic courts thanks to the component of strategic litigation supported by the project, respectively towards the rights of environment, access to public services, right to organization, access to justice. Some of these cases continue to last beyond the project period due to the delays and vacancies in judiciary. Thanks to such cases, the Constitutional Court that abrogated some of the provisions of the law on the registration of non-profit as unconstitutional. For the case of contestation of the judicial map from AHC, the Constitutional Court considered that it violates access to justice, but it didnt abrogate it with the argument of being proportional intervention due to the vacancies in judiciary. AHC plans to send the case to the European Court of Human Rights.
